question: Performance Grading Index, which is designed to catalyse transformational change in the field of school education, comprises of ____ indicators.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Performance Grading Index (PGI) is a comprehensive tool designed to assess the performance of states and union territories in the field of school education.
 
• The PGI comprises a total of 70 indicators that evaluate various aspects of school education.
 
• These indicators are grouped into two categories: Outcomes and Governance & Management.
 
• The PGI aims to provide insights into the strengths and areas for improvement in the education system, thereby catalyzing transformational change.
 
• The ultimate goal of the PGI is to ensure that the benefits of quality education reach all students across the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020:**

 
 
• NEP 2020 aims to transform India into a vibrant knowledge society and global knowledge superpower by making both school and college education more holistic, flexible, multidisciplinary, aligned to the needs of the 21st century, and aimed at bringing out the unique capabilities of each student.
 
• It emphasizes the need for early childhood care and education, foundational literacy and numeracy, curricular integration of essential subjects and skills, and the revision and revamping of all aspects of the education structure.
 
 
 
• **Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan:**
 
 
• Samagra Shiksha is an integrated scheme for school education extending from pre-school to class XII.
 
• The scheme aims to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education at all levels of school education.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education (RTE) Act:**
 
 
• The RTE Act, 2009 mandates free and compulsory education for children between the ages of 6 to 14 under Article 21A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It ensures that education is accessible and available to all children without discrimination.
 
 
 
• **Mid-Day Meal Scheme:**
 
 
• Launched in 1995, the Mid-Day Meal Scheme aims to enhance the enrollment, retention, and attendance of primary and upper primary students in government and government-aided schools.
 
• It provides nutritious meals to children, thereby addressing classroom hunger and enhancing their nutritional status.
